Guided ATV (quad bike) tours on Koh Samui run on private jungle tracks in the hills behind Maenam, in the central highlands and above Lipa Noi, and last from 30 minutes to about 4 hours. In 2026 a driver pays from 1,500 THB for 30 minutes or 1,800 THB for 1 hour, a passenger from 900 THB, and the 2–4 hour routes that add a waterfall, viewpoints and lunch cost 2,800–4,500 THB per driver. Most rides include a helmet, a guide riding in front and return transfer from the main beach areas; no motorbike licence is needed, but every operator sets a minimum age.

Routes: 30 minutes, 1–2 hours or half a day

All the tours start with a briefing and a practice lap on a flat circuit, then follow a guide in single file on plantation and jungle tracks. What changes with time is how far into the hills you get.

30–45 minutes: a taste

Short loops near the base, with mud, small climbs and a viewpoint or two. The Polaris 30-minute ride costs 1,500 THB per driver, and the Lipa Noi 30-minute ATV costs 1,800 THB per vehicle with a passenger riding free. Neither includes a hotel transfer, so the saving is smaller than it looks unless you have your own scooter or car.

1–2 hours: the classic ride

The 1-hour quad trail covers streams, red-dirt tracks and hill viewpoints; the 2-hour version adds a waterfall stop (it depends on recent rain) and one drink at a jungle bar. On the west coast the 1-hour and 1.5-hour Lipa Noi rides add the Lat Wanon waterfall and the Phu Lipa viewpoint. This is the length most first-timers enjoy most: long enough to get confident, short enough that your arms and back don't complain.

2.5–4 hours: viewpoints, the Magic Garden and lunch

The longer routes climb to the central ridge. The 1.5-hour and 2.5-hour Polaris rides include entry to the Secret Buddha Garden (Magic Garden) and the Tan Nim waterfall, and the 2.5-hour ride adds a Thai lunch at a mountain restaurant. The 4-hour Maenam mountain tour goes to the island's highest point with a hidden-waterfall swim and a buffet lunch, running roughly 09:00–15:00 hotel to hotel. These are the best value per hour, and the only way to reach the highlands on wheels without riding a scooter up roads that cause many of Samui's crashes.

Safety: what to expect and who should skip it

  • Helmet and guide. Every tour includes a helmet and a briefing, and a guide rides in front and sets the pace. Keep a full vehicle length from the one ahead; most minor accidents are riders running into each other on a downhill.
  • Licence. No motorbike licence is needed for these off-road tours on private tracks. Operators use a minimum age and a riding test on the practice circuit instead, and one Maenam operator asks buggy drivers for a car driving licence.
  • Insurance. Most of the tours include basic accident insurance, but damage you cause to the vehicle is your cost. Check that your travel insurance covers quad biking: many policies exclude it or need an add-on.
  • Health. Not suitable during pregnancy or with back, neck or heart problems. Rough tracks jar the spine, especially for passengers.
  • Heat. Morning starts are cooler. Drink water at every stop; the hills are humid even when the sky is grey.
  • No alcohol before you ride. Save the jungle-bar beer for the passenger.

Good to know: the nearest private hospitals with 24-hour emergency rooms are in Chaweng and Bophut. Save the ambulance number 1669 in your phone, and see hospitals and clinics on Koh Samui.

Children on ATV tours

Age rules differ by operator, so check the product before you book. On the quad trail, drivers must be 12 or older and pass a riding test, while children from 5 can ride as passengers with an adult. On the Lipa Noi ride, drivers must be 16, and children from 4 can be passengers; a driver with a child aged 4–11 pays 3,300 THB for an hour. On the Maenam mountain tour children under 10 ride as passengers only, and a shared ATV for an adult and a child under 10 costs 2,400 THB per person. For young children a buggy with a roll cage is the calmer choice.

Rainy-season riding

Samui's wet season is October to December, with the heaviest rain in November. The tours run all year, and some riders love the mud, but expect slippery climbs, deeper stream crossings and goggles that steam up. After a night of heavy rain, operators may shorten the route or close trails, and the waterfall stops become the highlight rather than an afterthought. From February to April the tracks are dry and dusty and the waterfalls run thin. Check the sky before you go: [kp_weather_now]. More on the seasons in Koh Samui weather by month and Koh Samui in November.

What to wear and bring

  • Closed shoes or trainers you don't mind ruining; no flip-flops.
  • Light long trousers or shorts you can get muddy, and a T-shirt that covers your shoulders.
  • Sunglasses or the goggles provided, and a face mask or buff for dust in the dry months.
  • Swimwear under your clothes if your route includes a waterfall.
  • A small dry bag for your phone; leave valuables at the hotel.
  • Cash for drinks and tips.

Across the market, a basic 1–2 hour ride with transfer starts at about 1,490 THB per rider in 2026, so the shortest rides cost much the same wherever you book. The difference is in what is included: check the transfer, lunch and entry fees before comparing prices.

Combine an ATV ride with the zipline

An ATV ride and a zipline fit into one day. The Tree Bridge zipline runs sessions at 09:30, 12:30 and 14:30, and the quad trail starts at 10:00 or 14:00, so take the 09:30 zipline and the 14:00 ride, with lunch in Maenam between. Both include transfer from the main beach areas. Compare courses on our Koh Samui zipline guide. If you'd rather see temples and waterfalls with someone else driving, the 4x4 jungle safari covers the interior in one day, and for a day on the water the Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB) runs all year.

Quads on the road: don't

Some shops offer quads for road use. We don't arrange it. The UK government's travel advice warns that rental motorbikes and scooters in tourist areas are often unregistered and can't be used legally on a public road, and the same applies to many rental quads. A quad is also unstable on Samui's steep, wet hill roads, insurers rarely cover it, and damage claims after road rentals are a known scam (see Koh Samui scams). To get around, read getting around Koh Samui or our scooter rental guide.

Where the bases are

Most ATV bases sit in the hills behind Maenam on the north coast, in the central highlands near the Secret Buddha Garden, and above Lipa Noi on the west coast. Exact addresses come with your voucher, because several bases are at the end of unnamed farm tracks. If you are staying in Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam or Nathon, the Lipa Noi base is the closest; from Chaweng, Bophut or Maenam, the Maenam rides include transfer.
